samples.label: Flowchart
samples.description: A request is checked for a signed-in visitor, then for a cached page; an uncached page is rendered first.
samples.source:
flowchart TD
  request[Incoming request] --> auth{Signed in?}
  auth -->|yes| cache{In the cache?}
  auth -->|no| login[Sign-in page]
  cache -->|yes| page[Cached page]
  cache -->|no| render[Render the page]
  render --> page

samples.label: Sequence
samples.description: A reader opens a guide. The site asks the build for the page, the build returns HTML with inline SVG, and the site sends it to the reader.
samples.source:
sequenceDiagram
  actor Reader
  participant Site as Documentation site
  participant Build
  Reader->>Site: Open the guide
  Site->>Build: Page not cached
  Build-->>Site: HTML with inline SVG
  Site-->>Reader: The page, diagrams included

samples.label: Class
samples.description: A document holds any number of blocks. Block is an interface that paragraphs and diagrams implement.

samples.label: State
samples.description: A page starts as a draft, goes to review, returns to draft when changes are requested, and is published, then archived.
samples.source:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Draft
  Draft --> Review: submit
  Review --> Draft: request changes
  Review --> Published: approve
  Published --> Archived: retire
  Archived --> [*]

samples.label: Entity relationship
samples.description: An author writes articles, an article contains sections, and a section shows diagrams.

samples.label: Git graph
samples.description: A docs branch leaves main, gains two commits and is merged back after a fix on main.
samples.source:
gitGraph
  commit id: "Initial"
  branch docs
  checkout docs
  commit id: "Add guide"
  commit id: "Add diagrams"
  checkout main
  commit id: "Fix build"
  merge docs
  commit id: "Release"

modes.source:
flowchart TD
  write[Write the guide] --> review{Review}
  review -->|Approved| publish[Publish]
  review -->|Changes requested| write
  publish --> announce[Announce the release]
modes.description: A guide is written and reviewed. Approval publishes it and the release is announced; requested changes send it back to writing.
